claim: smartctl -H reports overall device health where a failing status means the device has already failed or is predicting its own failure within the next 24 hours — the strongest single-value SMART alert a fleet agent can publish.
stance_target: agent SMART sensors should publish the smartctl -H health verdict as a primary binary_sensor, with its documented 'failure within 24 hours' semantics
scope_conditions: smartmontools on Linux; ATA/SATA and SCSI/SAS drives incl. SSDs
quoted_support: You can view a device's overall health with the -H flag. "If the device reports failing health status, this means either that the device has already failed, or that it is predicting its own failure within the next 24 hours. If this happens […] get your data off the disk and to someplace safe as soon as you can."

claim: smartd (systemd unit smartd.service, config /etc/smartd.conf) provides daemon-mode SMART monitoring with DEVICESCAN -a defaults, scheduled self-tests via '-s (S/../.././02|L/../../6/03)' (short daily 2-3am, extended Saturdays 3-4am), and temperature alerting via '-W 4,35,40' (log delta>=4C, log at 35C, warn at 40C).
stance_target: instead of the agent re-implementing SMART scheduling, it can either consume smartd events or adopt these documented threshold/schedule conventions

claim: smartd alert hooks execute via '-M exec <script>' (or scripts in /usr/share/smartmontools/smartd_warning.d/) with SMARTD_MESSAGE, SMARTD_FAILTYPE, and SMARTD_ADDRESS environment variables — the natural bridge from smartd to a MQTT-publishing fleet agent.
stance_target: ha-linux-agent can integrate disk-failure alerting without polling: a smartd -M exec hook publishing to MQTT preserves smartd's daemon-mode reliability
scope_conditions: smartd warning scripts must be executable
quoted_support:
The -M exec option causes a script to be executed ... #!/bin/sh
echo "$SMARTD_MESSAGE" | mail -s "$SMARTD_FAILTYPE" "$SMARTD_ADDRESS"

claim: smartd's -n standby,15,q directive prevents polling from spinning up sleeping disks (checks only if disk has been out of standby for 15+ minutes, quietly); default poll interval is 30 minutes via -i, and some devices lack ATA CHECK POWER STATUS support and ignore -n.
stance_target: agent SMART polling on kiosks/low-power hosts must respect disk standby states — naive polling wakes disks and defeats power management
quoted_support: Usually, in response to SMART commands issued by smartd, the disk platters are spun up. So if this option is not used, a disk which is in a low-power mode may be spun up and put into a higher-power mode when it is periodically polled by smartd.

claim: The Linux 'uas' USB driver can disable SAT transfers, preventing smartmontools from communicating with SATA devices behind USB bridges — a fleet-wide agent must tolerate SMART being unreadable on some hardware rather than treating it as host failure.
stance_target: agent error taxonomy: distinguish 'SMART unsupported/unreachable on this device' from 'sensor failure' to avoid false fleet alarms
scope_conditions: USB-attached SATA devices with uas driver
quoted_support: In certain situations the Linux "uas" driver disables SAT transfers, which prevents smartmontools (and other tools, e.g. hdparm) from communicating properly with the attached SATA device.

claim: Scrutiny is catalogued by ArchWiki as 'WebUI for smartd S.M.A.R.T monitoring' (github.com/AnalogJ/scrutiny), and update-smart-drivedb refreshes drivedb.h so new drive models are recognised — the operational companion tools around smartctl/smartd.
stance_target: drivedb freshness matters for new-drive attribute decoding; Scrutiny is the established hub UI the agent ecosystem coexists with
quoted_support:
scrutiny — WebUI for smartd S.M.A.R.T monitoring.
https://github.com/AnalogJ/scrutiny
